note: Refreshed every week by the program's research task. Each item says what changed, why it matters to a data engineer or architect, and how to test the claim yourself.

items.title: Agents that run one task for more than a day
items.summary: Product teams report long-horizon agents that keep working for hours or days on one task, using progress files, checkpoints and a router that picks a model per step.
items.why: This is harness engineering, not a new model: budgets, checkpoints and evidence decide whether a long run is useful. You build the same pieces in modules AI 1 and AI 3.
items.try: Add a progress file and a resume step to your Lab 2 agent, kill it mid-run, and check it continues without repeating work.

items.title: Small, cheap models with very long context as subagents
items.summary: Small models with context windows near a million tokens make it practical to read a whole repo or a day of logs and hand a short summary to a larger model. Claude Haiku 5.5 is one example.
items.why: Routing reading and triage to a cheap model and keeping the expensive model for decisions is the biggest credit saver after caching.
items.try: In Lab 3, send triage to the cheapest model and compare accuracy and cost per 100 runs with the large model.

items.title: Always-on agents
items.summary: Agents that keep working toward a goal between conversations, waking on a schedule or an event.
items.why: Same engineering as a scheduled pipeline: idempotency, budgets, alerting and a human approval step for anything that changes production.
items.try: Turn your Lab 4 automation into an event-triggered run and add an approval gate before it writes anything.

items.title: Agent swarms: many agents in parallel
items.summary: Some open models and frameworks are reported to coordinate very large numbers of parallel agents.
items.why: Parallel agents only help when the subtasks are independent. Measure cost per useful result, not the number of agents.
items.try: Split one task from Lab 10 into 3 parallel subagents and compare time, tokens and accuracy with a single agent.

items.title: Teams measure agents by cost per merged change
items.summary: Teams now judge coding and operations agents by cost per merged pull request or per resolved incident, not by demo quality.
items.why: This is the eval habit from module AI 2: define the outcome, measure it on a fixed set, and track cost next to quality.
items.try: Add cost per resolved case to your Lab 11 eval report.

items.title: MCP is the standard way to give agents tools
items.summary: The Model Context Protocol is supported by most agent clients, so one read-only server can serve many agents.
items.why: For a data platform, an MCP server is the safe front door: read-only SQL, row limits and audit logs in one place.
items.try: Run Lab 9 and confirm that the server refuses DROP and caps rows.
